jobs.title: Director, Solution Architecture – Information Technology
jobs.description:
Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. We believe in what we do—and place trust in our employees to deliver our vision.

Working at Alberta Blue Cross® means having a career where you’ll be recognized for your contributions. We value diversity, encourage our team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance and provide opportunities for career growth.

Overview

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead a team of 10+ Solution Architects at Alberta Blue Cross. Reporting to the Chief Architect, this senior leadership role combines strong people leadership with deep, practical technology solution architecture experience. The Director leads Solution Architecture practice and ensures initiatives have implementable, delivery-ready designs aligned to enterprise architecture direction, approved portfolio target states, and portfolio modernization roadmaps.

The Director translates approved architecture direction into technology solutions that delivery teams can build, integrate, operate, and evolve. The role brings credible technical leadership across applications, integration and APIs, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure, balancing business outcomes with feasibility, performance, resiliency, privacy, cost, and maintainability. The Director guides complex design decisions and supports architecture through implementation and transition to operations.

Within the proposed Enterprise Architect target-state operating model, Enterprise Architects set enterprise direction and guardrails; Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures and modernization roadmaps; and Solution Architects design and guide implementation within those boundaries. The Director of Solution Architecture leads the people, capacity, technical quality, and operating practices of the Solution Architecture team. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, Domain Architects, and especially Portfolio Architects to connect delivery decisions to enterprise direction and portfolio roadmaps.

Success in this role is achieved by:

Leading, coaching, developing, and aligning a team of 10+ Solution Architects with clear priorities, accountability, and a collaborative technical culture. Most of the Solution Architects are already in place but additional resources may be required depending on demand. These Solution Architects are positioned as generalists who work across various technologies.
Applying deep technology solution architecture experience to produce practical, secure, resilient, and delivery-ready designs for complex initiatives.
Managing architecture demand, team capacity, assignments, and skills development across portfolios and delivery priorities.
Partnering with Portfolio Architects to align solution designs, dependencies, transition states, and technical feasibility with approved portfolio roadmaps.
Collaborating with Enterprise Architects, in their respective specializations, to apply enterprise guardrails, reuse enterprise capabilities and data, and resolve design risks through formal governance.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Lead and mature the Solution Architecture practice, including design methods, review practices, documentation, engagement models, and implementation support.
Lead a team of 10+ Solution Architects, including recruitment, onboarding, coaching, development planning, performance management, succession planning, and technical capability development.
Manage solution architecture demand and capacity; assign architects to initiatives with Portfolio Architects and delivery leaders, balancing priorities, complexity, dependencies, and skills.
Provide senior technical leadership for complex solutions across application, integration and API, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure domains; challenge assumptions and guide design trade-offs.
Establish and monitor solution architecture measures for design readiness, review turnaround, guardrail alignment, reuse, technical risk, and implementation conformance.
Ensure solution designs leverage enterprise data and approved shared platforms, services, reference architectures, and patterns; address data ownership, quality, lineage, access, privacy, and integration with relevant domain specialists.
Oversee initiative-level architecture from discovery and options assessment through design, implementation support, and operational handover, maintaining traceability to business and non-functional requirements.
Partner closely with Portfolio Architects to translate portfolio target architectures, transition states, architecture runway, and modernization roadmaps into implementable solution designs; provide feasibility, dependency, and risk input for roadmap decisions.
Coach Solution Architects in system design, technology evaluation, integration, cloud adoption, secure design, cost trade-offs, and clear communication of technical decisions.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, and Domain Architects to interpret guardrails, obtain specialist input, and submit proposed patterns or exceptions through established governance.
Identify solution-level technical debt, integration constraints, implementation risks, duplication, and roadmap impacts; agree mitigation actions with portfolio, delivery, and platform stakeholders.
Work with business owners, engineering, delivery, security, privacy, data, platform, infrastructure and operations teams, and vendors to validate feasibility and guide implementation of approved designs.
Maintain transparent architecture decision records and escalate material exceptions, cross-portfolio conflicts, or changes to approved target states and sequencing; do not bypass enterprise or portfolio governance.

POSITION SCOPE

Reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice, with people leadership for a team of 10+ Solution Architects.
Provides technical leadership and design assurance for initiatives across business and technology portfolios, from early discovery through implementation and transition to operations.
Owns solution architecture practice methods, team capacity and assignments, design quality, solution-level deliverables, peer reviews, and practice effectiveness reporting.
Provides direct leadership, coaching, prioritization, performance management, and career development for Solution Architects; builds technical depth and leadership capability across the team.
Is accountable for the Solution Architecture capability and design assurance, not enterprise architecture policy, portfolio roadmap ownership, project delivery management, software engineering management, or production operations.

ACCOUNTABILITY BOUNDARIES AND ROLE CLARITY:

The Director of Solution Architecture reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice and a team of 10+ Solution Architects. The Director is accountable for people leadership, capacity planning, technical capability, design quality, and consistent solution architecture engagement across portfolios.
Enterprise Architects define enterprise-wide architectural direction, principles, standards, reference architectures, target states, and guardrails. The Director of Enterprise Architecture leads the EA function and its governance and domain architecture capability. The Director of Solution Architecture applies that direction to initiative-level design and contributes delivery insight, reusable patterns, and improvement proposals; the role does not assume enterprise policy ownership or leadership of Domain Architects.
Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures, transition states, modernization roadmaps, and architecture runway. The Director of Solution Architecture partners with Portfolio Architects to align architect assignments and solution designs with roadmap priorities and approved sequencing. The team provides technical feasibility, integration, dependency, and implementation feedback that may prompt roadmap changes; ownership of portfolio roadmaps and sequencing remains with Portfolio Architects.
Solution Architects own solution design decisions for assigned initiatives within approved enterprise and portfolio guardrails. They produce and maintain delivery-ready architecture deliverables, guide implementation, and support transition to operations. The Director provides technical coaching, peer review, design assurance, and escalation support without removing the assigned architect’s design accountability. Material exceptions follow formal governance rather than unilateral approval by the Director or Solution Architects.
Enterprise Architects provide specialist design authority and guidance. Delivery and engineering leaders remain accountable for implementation, project execution, and engineering management; platform and operations leaders retain operational accountabilities. This separation connects enterprise direction, portfolio roadmaps, solution design, and delivery while keeping decision rights clear.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

Lead and mature the Solution Architecture practice as a delivery-enabling capability within the proposed EA operating model.
Own consistent solution design methods, architecture deliverables, peer reviews, and design assurance from discovery through implementation.
Lead and develop a team of 10+ Solution Architects, including recruitment, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and career development.
Manage architecture demand, capacity, assignments, and reporting in partnership with Portfolio Architects, EPMO, and delivery leaders.
Ensure solution designs align to approved enterprise guardrails, portfolio target states, transition states, and roadmap sequencing.
Provide deep technical leadership and constructive challenge on complex application, integration, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure designs.
Promote reuse of enterprise data, approved services, platforms, and patterns while meeting security, privacy, performance, resilience, operability, and cost requirements.
Make solution-level risks, dependencies, technical debt, and roadmap impacts visible; support mitigation and escalate decisions outside approved design authority.
Coordinate Enterprise, Portfolio, Domain, and Solution Architects with engineering, delivery, platform, operations, and vendor teams to guide implementation without assuming their distinct accountabilities.
Maintain business-to-design traceability, architecture decision records, implementation feedback, and operational handover readiness.
Measure practice effectiveness and improve design readiness, review responsiveness, guardrail alignment, reuse, and implementation conformance.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES:

Solution designs are delivery-ready, traceable to business and non-functional requirements, and aligned with enterprise guardrails and portfolio target states.
Practice reporting shows design readiness, timely architecture engagement and reviews, implementation conformance, reuse, and transparent technical risk and exception management.
Architecture assignments, capacity plans, role expectations, and development plans support a team of 10+ Solution Architects across portfolio priorities.
Solution decisions support portfolio modernization roadmaps and transition states; feasibility, dependencies, and delivery constraints inform Portfolio Architect roadmap decisions.
Solutions avoid unnecessary duplication and unmanaged technical debt through reuse of enterprise data, platforms, services, and approved patterns.
Business, portfolio, engineering, and delivery stakeholders receive practical solution options, clear trade-offs, and timely design

jobs.description:
Job Description

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If contacted in relation to a job opportunity or testing, you should advise the member of the Talent Acquisition team in a timely fashion of any disabilities that requires accommodation measures in order to enable you to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner.

Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

No agency or telephone inquiries please.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Finance based in Canada.

As the first finance leader, you will have the opportunity to build and shape the financial function of a fast-growing company operating at the intersection of aviation, robotics, and autonomous technology. You will take ownership of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and strategic financial planning. Working closely with executive leadership and department heads, you will translate operational and commercial decisions into clear financial insights that support sustainable growth. You will also play a key role in managing cross-border financial operations across multiple international entities. This position combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution, offering significant autonomy and the opportunity to establish scalable financial processes as the business expands globally.

Accountabilities

Accounting and Financial Reporting: Own monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with US GAAP, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timely reporting.
Multi-Entity Financial Management: Manage financial consolidation, foreign currency accounting, and intercompany transactions across US, Canadian, and UK entities.
Revenue Recognition and Controls: Oversee revenue recognition processes, accounts payable, and accounts receivable while establishing effective financial controls and reporting procedures.
Tax and Audit Coordination: Coordinate tax compliance, external accounting support, and audit preparation with specialized external advisers.
Budgeting and Financial Planning: Lead the annual budgeting process, maintain rolling forecasts, and develop financial models aligned with business objectives and operational priorities.
Cash Flow Management: Maintain short- and long-term cash forecasts, covering working capital requirements, capital expenditures, and future financing needs.
Business and Commercial Analysis: Evaluate customer economics, deployment costs, pricing strategies, and expansion scenarios to support informed business decisions.
Financial Systems and Automation: Improve accounting and financial planning infrastructure, including ERP selection or implementation, and leverage automation and AI tools to streamline workflows while maintaining appropriate controls.
Financing and Fundraising Support: Evaluate debt and equipment financing opportunities, prepare financial due diligence materials, and support fundraising activities in collaboration with leadership and external advisers.
Strategic Business Partnership: Work closely with department leaders to assess the financial implications of hiring plans, deployment strategies, investments, and other operational decisions.

Requirements

Professional Experience: At least 8 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including direct ownership of financial closing processes and reporting within a growing organization.
Professional Qualifications: CPA designation or an equivalent professional accounting qualification, with strong knowledge of US GAAP and ASC 606 revenue recognition standards.
Hands-On Finance Leadership: Experience operating independently within a small finance team or as the primary accounting owner, with the ability to establish processes while personally managing day-to-day execution.
Financial Planning Expertise: Demonstrated experience managing budgets, cash flow forecasts, financial models, and variance analysis, with the ability to translate operational assumptions into financial recommendations.
International Accounting Experience: Strong understanding of multi-entity accounting, cross-border financial operations, US financial reporting, and coordination with external tax advisers.
Technical Skills: Advanced spreadsheet capabilities, familiarity with financial systems, and the ability to improve reporting processes through technology and automation.
Analytical and Strategic Thinking: Strong financial judgment and the ability to evaluate complex business scenarios, identify risks, and provide actionable insights.
Communication and Collaboration: Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with executive leadership, operational teams, and external financial partners.
Autonomy and Ownership: A proactive, detail-oriented approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and build scalable financial infrastructure in a dynamic environment.

Nice To Have

Experience working in a venture capital-backed company, particularly in robotics, hardware, industrial automation, or logistics.
Familiarity with inventory management, hardware-related financial operations, or Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) business models.
Experience selecting, implementing, or optimizing ERP systems and modern financial technology tools.
Previous involvement in equity fundraising, debt facilities, equipment financing, or financial due diligence processes.

Benefits

Competitive annual compensation: CAD $250,000–$300,000.
Leadership opportunity: Build and lead the finance function as the organization's first dedicated finance hire.
Strategic influence: Work directly with executive leadership and contribute to major financial and operational decisions.
International exposure: Oversee financial operations across Canadian, US, and UK entities.
Remote work: Enjoy the flexibility of a remote position based in Canada.
Professional growth: Develop your expertise in a high-growth, venture-backed environment at the intersection of aviation, robotics, and autonomous technology.
Ownership and autonomy: Establish financial processes, systems, and strategies that will support the company's long-term expansion.
Innovation-driven environment: Explore modern financial systems, automation, and AI-powered tools to improve finance operations.

Reporting to the Chief Architect, this senior leadership role combines strong people leadership with deep, practical technology solution architecture experience. The Director leads Solution Architecture practice and ensures initiatives have implementable, delivery-ready designs aligned to enterprise architecture direction, approved portfolio target states, and portfolio modernization roadmaps.

The Director translates approved architecture direction into technology solutions that delivery teams can build, integrate, operate, and evolve. The role brings credible technical leadership across applications, integration and APIs, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure, balancing business outcomes with feasibility, performance, resiliency, privacy, cost, and maintainability. The Director guides complex design decisions and supports architecture through implementation and transition to operations.

Within the proposed Enterprise Architect target-state operating model, Enterprise Architects set enterprise direction and guardrails; Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures and modernization roadmaps; and Solution Architects design and guide implementation within those boundaries. The Director of Solution Architecture leads the people, capacity, technical quality, and operating practices of the Solution Architecture team. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, Domain Architects, and especially Portfolio Architects to connect delivery decisions to enterprise direction and portfolio roadmaps.

Success in this role is achieved by:

Leading, coaching, developing, and aligning a team of 10+ Solution Architects with clear priorities, accountability, and a collaborative technical culture. Most of the Solution Architects are already in place but additional resources may be required depending on demand. These Solution Architects are positioned as generalists who work across various technologies.
Applying deep technology solution architecture experience to produce practical, secure, resilient, and delivery-ready designs for complex initiatives.
Managing architecture demand, team capacity, assignments, and skills development across portfolios and delivery priorities.
Partnering with Portfolio Architects to align solution designs, dependencies, transition states, and technical feasibility with approved portfolio roadmaps.
Collaborating with Enterprise Architects, in their respective specializations, to apply enterprise guardrails, reuse enterprise capabilities and data, and resolve design risks through formal governance.

Lead and mature the Solution Architecture practice, including design methods, review practices, documentation, engagement models, and implementation support.
Lead a team of 10+ Solution Architects, including recruitment, onboarding, coaching, development planning, performance management, succession planning, and technical capability development.
Manage solution architecture demand and capacity; assign architects to initiatives with Portfolio Architects and delivery leaders, balancing priorities, complexity, dependencies, and skills.
Provide senior technical leadership for complex solutions across application, integration and API, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure domains; challenge assumptions and guide design trade-offs.
Establish and monitor solution architecture measures for design readiness, review turnaround, guardrail alignment, reuse, technical risk, and implementation conformance.
Ensure solution designs leverage enterprise data and approved shared platforms, services, reference architectures, and patterns; address data ownership, quality, lineage, access, privacy, and integration with relevant domain specialists.
Oversee initiative-level architecture from discovery and options assessment through design, implementation support, and operational handover, maintaining traceability to business and non-functional requirements.
Partner closely with Portfolio Architects to translate portfolio target architectures, transition states, architecture runway, and modernization roadmaps into implementable solution designs; provide feasibility, dependency, and risk input for roadmap decisions.
Coach Solution Architects in system design, technology evaluation, integration, cloud adoption, secure design, cost trade-offs, and clear communication of technical decisions.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, and Domain Architects to interpret guardrails, obtain specialist input, and submit proposed patterns or exceptions through established governance.

Work with business owners, engineering, delivery, security, privacy, data, platform, infrastructure and operations teams, and vendors to validate feasibility and guide implementation of approved designs.

POSITION SCOPE

Reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice, with people leadership for a team of 10+ Solution Architects.
Provides technical leadership and design assurance for initiatives across business and technology portfolios, from early discovery through implementation and transition to operations.
Owns solution architecture practice methods, team capacity and assignments, design quality, solution-level deliverables, peer reviews, and practice effectiveness reporting.
Provides direct leadership, coaching, prioritization, performance management, and career development for Solution Architects; builds technical depth and leadership capability across the team.
Is accountable for the Solution Architecture capability and design assurance, not enterprise architecture policy, portfolio roadmap ownership, project delivery management, software engineering management, or production operations.

ACCOUNTABILITY BOUNDARIES AND ROLE CLARITY:

The Director of Solution Architecture reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice and a team of 10+ Solution Architects. The Director is accountable for people leadership, capacity planning, technical capability, design quality, and consistent solution architecture engagement across portfolios.
Enterprise Architects define enterprise-wide architectural direction, principles, standards, reference architectures, target states, and guardrails. The Director of Enterprise Architecture leads the EA function and its governance and domain architecture capability. The Director of Solution Architecture applies that direction to initiative-level design and contributes delivery insight, reusable patterns, and improvement proposals; the role does not assume enterprise policy ownership or leadership of Domain Architects.
Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures, transition states, modernization roadmaps, and architecture runway. The Director of Solution Architecture partners with Portfolio Architects to align architect assignments and solution designs with roadmap priorities and approved sequencing. The team provides technical feasibility, integration, dependency, and implementation feedback that may prompt roadmap changes; ownership of portfolio roadmaps and sequencing remains with Portfolio Architects.
Solution Architects own solution design decisions for assigned initiatives within approved enterprise and portfolio guardrails. They produce and maintain delivery-ready architecture deliverables, guide implementation, and support transition to operations. The Director provides technical coaching, peer review, design assurance, and escalation support without removing the assigned architect’s design accountability. Material exceptions follow formal governance rather than unilateral approval by the Director or Solution Architects.
Enterprise Architects provide specialist design authority and guidance. Delivery and engineering leaders remain accountable for implementation, project execution, and engineering management; platform and operations leaders retain operational accountabilities. This separation connects enterprise direction, portfolio roadmaps, solution design, and delivery while keeping decision rights clear.

Measure practice effectiveness and improve design readiness, review responsiveness, guardrail alignment, reuse, and implementation conformance.

Solution designs are delivery-ready, traceable to business and non-functional requirements, and aligned with enterprise guardrails and portfolio target states.
